## Conflicts

| temp-id | parties | contradiction | proposed resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| CF-286 | WS-B4 vs WS-B1 (ADR-0026/ADR-0027 event table and envelope) | B4 needs three additional event classes (`lifecycle.branch.opened/disposed`, `action.environment.restored`, `lifecycle.replay.started/finished`) and an optional `scope.branch_id` for intra-run branches; B1's table has `run.forked`, `head.moved`, `rolled_back` and `environment.snapshot` but no branch-disposition or restore class | Additive amendment to ADR-0026's amendment log at Phase 2 synthesis; `branch_id` is derived (the branch root's `EventId`) and stamped into `scope` for projection speed only; persistence policy `ledger` for all four. |
| CF-287 | WS-B4 vs WS-B2 (ADR-0030 lifecycle) | ADR-0030's lifecycle has no state for "prepared but must not run inside this branch"; B4 needs a non-terminal `deferred` phase between `prepared` and `committed`/`refused` | Amend ADR-0030 additively: `deferred` is non-terminal, entered by `action.effect.deferred`, left only to `committed` (after fresh authorization) or `refused`; "every commit resolves" is untouched because a deferred effect is never committed. |
| CF-288 | WS-B4 vs WS-L4 (ADR-0038 `NondeterminismDeclaration.source`) | ADR-0038's five sources omit `randomness`, `environment_state`, `human_input`, `external_service`, which B4's replay verdict must distinguish | Extend the enum additively (nine values); bundles written under the five-value set remain valid (unknown sources default to `confined_to_events = false`). |
| CF-289 | WS-B4 vs WS-A1 §6.3 / OpenHands precedent (S-110) | WS-A1 describes the ledger as "≈ OpenHands EventLog"; OpenHands' `fork()` shares one live workspace between the source and the fork, which B4 classifies as the SF2/SF3 failure signature | Keep the analogy for the *log*; B4 makes trace-only forks a restricted `env_binding = trace_only` mode limited to `read_only` effects. No change to WS-A1's ADRs. |
| CF-290 | WS-B4 vs doc 3 §2.2 / doc 2 §5.5 wording ("checkpoints and deterministic environment snapshots improve replay") | Environment snapshots make *reconstruction* and *re-execution from a prefix* deterministic; they do not make *replay of decisions* deterministic (ADR-0028) | Spec §7.2-5 text for R-2.2.4 should say "snapshots improve reconstruction and re-execution; decision replay is a declared variant capability"; consistent with ADR-0028. |

## Ontology terms

| term | definition | notes |
|---|---|---|
| branch (intra-run / inter-run) | A continuation of a run from a fork point. *Intra-run*: a `parent_event_id` subtree under the run's single writer lease, opened by `lifecycle.branch.opened` and promoted/discarded by `lifecycle.head.moved`. *Inter-run*: a new run with `forked_from` (ADR-0027 §6). Both carry a branch record. | WS-B4; consumes ADR-0027 lineage and HEAD; WS-F3's delegation is an inter-run branch with `branch_kind = delegation`. |
| fork point / coherent fork point | `(run_id, seq)` from which a branch continues. *Coherent* iff no model-call scope opened at or before `seq` is open and every effect scope opened at or before `seq` is terminal, `deferred`, or detached; turn boundaries and effect terminals are always coherent. Forking elsewhere is `ForkPointNotCoherent` or coerced to the nearest earlier coherent seq with a synthesized `lifecycle.turn.finished{stop_reason: forked}`. | WS-B4; precedent codex `ForkSnapshot`, Claude SDK `resume_drops_turn`. |
| branch record | `BranchRecord{branch_id, fork_point, source_head_hash, branch_kind ∈ {speculative, counterfactual, exploration, recovery, delegation}, env_binding ∈ {snapshot, trace_only}, replay_mode, intervention_ref?, speculation_policy_ref, budget_id, permissions, seed, provenance, disposition?}` — the payload of `lifecycle.run.forked` / `lifecycle.branch.opened`. | WS-B4. |
| branch disposition | The single terminal fact about a branch: `promoted{at_seq} | discarded{reason, restored_to, compensated[], uncompensable[]} | abandoned{reason} | merged{into_run_id, merge_ref}`; recorded by `lifecycle.branch.disposed`. | WS-B4; `merged` semantics owned by WS-F3. |
| environment snapshot (`EnvSnapshot`) | A content-addressed record of an environment handle's covered state at an `EventRef`: `{snapshot_id, env_handle, taken_at, kind ∈ {workspace_tree, fs_layer, process_image, full_vm}, coverage, uncaptured[], cost, idp}`; referenced by `action.environment.snapshot`, never an event payload; restored by `action.environment.restored` into a fresh handle. | WS-B4 contract; WS-B5 mechanism per kind (OQ-089). `snapshot_id` uses the ADR-0036 tree rule for `workspace_tree` and `foreign_digest` claims otherwise. |
| coverage / uncaptured | The declared subset of environment state an `EnvSnapshot` restores (`workspace_files, filesystem, processes, memory, devices`) and the list of state it cannot (`network_connections, wall_clock, entropy, external_services, secrets`, plus nondeterminism sources). Coverage bounds the `reversible` effect class. | WS-B4; Firecracker (S-481) supplies the canonical `uncaptured` items for VM snapshots. |
| trace-only fork | A branch with `env_binding = trace_only`: the event log forks but the environment is shared live; admitted only with `SpeculationPolicy.allow_classes = {read_only}`. | WS-B4; the restricted form of the OpenHands `fork()` behaviour (CF-289). |
| atomic trace–environment coupling | The invariant that a branch with `env_binding = snapshot` is created with an `EnvSnapshot` whose `taken_at.seq` equals the fork point and runs on a fresh handle restored from it. | WS-B4; Shepherd "the agent and its environment are forked atomically"; violation = SF2/SF3 (S-476). |
| speculative branch | A branch with `branch_kind = speculative` whose effects are contained by the speculation policy: `read_only` and covered `workspace_local reversible` effects run; `compensable` only by opt-in with a registered compensator; everything else is deferred. | WS-B4. |
| speculation policy | `SpeculationPolicy{allow_classes, require_compensator, max_concurrent_branches, budget_fraction, coverage_required, defer_irreversible = true}` — a `HarnessRule`-class artifact (MUST-data); `defer_irreversible` is not overridable by any layer. | WS-B4; ADR-0024 rung MUST-data. |
| deferred effect | An effect in the non-terminal phase `deferred` (entered from `prepared` by `action.effect.deferred{reason ∈ {speculative_branch, awaiting_promotion}}`), never committed inside its branch; released to `committed` on promotion after fresh authorization, or `refused` on discard. The model sees an explicit "deferred" observation. | WS-B4; amends ADR-0030 (CF-287). |
| rewind note | A typed `Text` leaf (`authority = kernel`) rendered into the model-facing view after a rollback or discard: `{rolled_back_to, persisted_external_effects[], compensated[], deferred_released[], attempt_summary_ref?}`. | WS-B4; D1 renders (OQ-320); precedent AgentRewind rewind memory, codex `<turn_aborted>`. |
| replay mode | `reconstruct_reexecute` (default: prefix reconstructed from ledger + snapshot, suffix re-executed with fresh samples) or `deterministic` (a declaring variant is driven by recorded inputs; no effect is dispatched). Recorded on every branch and every branch-derived results row. | WS-B4; ADR-0028 consequence. |
| replay validity report | `ReplayValidityReport{mode ∈ {deterministic, re_executed, degraded, invalid}, variant_declares_deterministic_replay, sources[], env, model{fingerprint_match}, external_dependencies[], reasons[]}` — a pure projection over the branch record, the source prefix and the bundle; the mode is the minimum over sources. | WS-B4; feeds WS-I7/I2/I3; caps the ADR-0038 reproducibility level. |
| nondeterminism source | `{provider_sampling, wall_clock, randomness, network, filesystem_order, concurrency, environment_state, human_input, external_service}` — each either confined to events (recorded, substitutable) or declared. Extends the ADR-0038 `NondeterminismDeclaration.source` set. | WS-B4 (amendment to WS-L4's term; CF-288). |
| intervention record | `InterventionRecord{kind ∈ {definition_diff, profile_diff, response_substitution, observation_substitution, decision_override, budget_change, permission_change}, target, payload_ref, earliest_affected_seq, coupling_assumption ∈ {weak, declared_strong}, hypothesis, provenance}` — what a counterfactual branch changes relative to its source. | WS-B4; consumed by WS-I7; `HirDiff` (ADR-0017) is the payload for definition/profile kinds. |
| counterfactual branch / factual re-execution arm | A branch with `branch_kind = counterfactual` and an intervention record; admissible only when paired with `n ≥ k` factual re-executions from the same fork point and snapshot under a matched suffix budget, seeds as replicates, distributions reported with `replay_mode`. | WS-B4 (design), WS-I7 (`k`, margin, statistic — OQ-323). |
